title: Micron Says Taiwan Work Is Normal After Report of Halted Taoyuan Plant
summaryZh: 美光稱台灣營運正常，傳桃園新廠因勞資爭議喊停
summaryHi: माइक्रॉन ने कहा ताइवान में काम सामान्य, श्रम विवाद के बीच ताओयुआन प्लांट रुकने की ख़बर
summaryEs: Micron dice que opera con normalidad en Taiwán tras informes de que frenó una planta en Taoyuan por un conflicto laboral
summaryJa: マイクロン、台湾事業は通常通りと説明　桃園新工場は労使対立で停止と報道
summaryKo: 마이크론 "대만 운영 정상"…노사 갈등 속 타오위안 신공장 중단 보도
summaryEn: Micron says its Taiwan operations are normal after a report that it halted a new Taoyuan plant amid a labour dispute.
paragraphs: US memory chipmaker Micron Technology insisted on Thursday that its Taiwan operations were continuing as normal, following a Bloomberg report that it had shelved plans for a new plant in Taoyuan amid a labour dispute.

The report said Micron had halted an investment of between US$3 billion and US$4.5 billion in the facility, which was meant to produce DRAM and high-bandwidth memory chips using advanced equipment from ASML. Observers worry the move could deepen a global shortage of memory chips. Taiwan accounts for about 60% of Micron's conventional memory output, according to Bloomberg.

In its statement, Micron did not directly address the reported suspension. Instead, it said it was confident it could keep its Taoyuan operations stable without disrupting customers, and that it would keep negotiating with the local union in talks facilitated by the Taoyuan City government.

The Taoyuan union is demanding a specific profit-sharing scheme. It has been authorised to strike and staged a symbolic 24-hour walkout on October 22, but says it remains open to dialogue. Micron settled with its Taichung union in late October; that union represents most of its employees in Taiwan.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs said it would help facilitate negotiations if needed, describing Micron as one of Taiwan's most important foreign investors, with cumulative investment of NT$1.6 trillion.
Micron is a big American company. It makes memory chips for computers and phones. Many of its factories are in Taiwan.
A news report said Micron stopped its plan for a new factory in Taoyuan. The factory was going to cost US$3 to 4.5 billion.
Some workers in Taoyuan are not happy. Their union wants a better way to share the company's profits. On October 22, they stopped work for one day.
On Thursday, Micron said its work in Taiwan is normal. It did not say yes or no about the new factory. It will keep talking with the union, and the Taoyuan city government is helping.
Micron has about 3,000 workers in Taoyuan and 12,300 in Taichung. In October, it made a deal with the workers in Taichung.

paragraphs: American chipmaker Micron said on Thursday that its business in Taiwan is running normally. The statement came after a Bloomberg report said the company had stopped plans for a new factory in Taoyuan because of a disagreement with workers.

According to the report, Micron had planned to spend US$3 to 4.5 billion on the new site. The factory would make advanced memory chips, including HBM chips used in AI. Some people fear that the decision could make the world's shortage of memory chips worse.

Micron did not answer the report directly. It said it was confident it could keep its Taoyuan factory stable without causing problems for customers. It also said it would continue talks with the Taoyuan workers' union, with help from the city government.

The union wants a special plan to share company profits with staff. Its members have the right to strike, and they held a 24-hour strike on October 22. However, they say they are still ready to talk. In late October, Micron reached an agreement with its union in Taichung.
Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs said it would help both sides if needed. It called Micron one of Taiwan's most important foreign investors.

paragraphs: Micron Technology sought to reassure customers on Thursday, stating that its operations in Taiwan remained unaffected after Bloomberg reported that the US memory giant had put plans for a new Taoyuan plant on hold amid an unresolved labour dispute.

According to Bloomberg, Micron has suspended an investment of US$3 billion to US$4.5 billion in the facility, which was earmarked for DRAM and high-bandwidth memory production and was to be equipped with cutting-edge ASML machinery. The news has fuelled fears that an already acute global memory shortage could intensify, given that Taiwan produces roughly 60% of the company's conventional memory chips.

Pointedly sidestepping the question of the suspension, Micron said it was confident of maintaining stable operations in Taoyuan without disruption to customers, and pledged to continue negotiations with the local union, facilitated by the Taoyuan City government.

At the heart of the dispute is the union's demand for a specific profit-sharing programme. Although its members are authorised to strike and held a symbolic 24-hour stoppage on October 22, union leaders say they remain willing to negotiate. The company reached a deal in late October with its far larger Taichung union, whose roughly 11,000 members make up the bulk of its Taiwan workforce.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs signalled that it stood ready to facilitate talks, underlining Micron's status as one of the country's foremost foreign investors, with cumulative investment amounting to NT$1.6 trillion.
sentZh: 美光科技星期四試圖安撫客戶，表示其台灣營運未受影響；此前彭博社報導，這家美國記憶體巨頭因一場懸而未決的勞資糾紛，已暫緩桃園新廠的計畫。
據彭博社報導，美光已暫停對該廠房30億至45億美元的投資，該廠原定用於生產DRAM和高頻寬記憶體，並將配備艾司摩爾的尖端設備。
這則消息加深外界憂慮，擔心原本已十分嚴重的全球記憶體短缺會進一步惡化，因為美光約60%的傳統記憶體晶片是在台灣生產。
美光刻意迴避暫停一事，只表示有信心維持桃園營運穩定、不影響客戶，並承諾在桃園市政府協調下繼續與當地工會協商。
糾紛的核心是工會要求一套特定的分紅方案。
雖然工會成員已獲授權罷工，並在10月22日舉行象徵性的24小時停工，工會領袖表示仍願意協商。
公司已在10月下旬與規模大得多的台中工會達成協議，該工會約11,000名會員佔美光台灣員工的大多數。
經濟部表示已準備好協助促成協商，並強調美光是台灣首屈一指的外國投資者之一，累計投資金額達新台幣1.6兆元。

paragraphs: The American semiconductor manufacturer Micron Technology announced on Thursday that its Taiwanese operations were functioning normally, in response to a media report suggesting that it had suspended plans to construct a new facility in Taoyuan.

The report, published by Bloomberg, claimed that a proposed investment worth between US$3 billion and US$4.5 billion had been halted as a consequence of a labour dispute. The plant was intended to manufacture advanced memory chips, which are essential components in artificial intelligence systems. Industry observers are concerned that this development could exacerbate the existing worldwide shortage of such chips.

Notably, Micron's statement neither confirmed nor denied the suspension. The company expressed confidence that it could sustain stable production in Taoyuan without affecting its clients, and it committed to further negotiations with the local trade union, assisted by municipal officials.

The union, which represents around 2,400 of the 3,000 employees in Taoyuan, is seeking a particular profit-sharing arrangement. Despite having held a symbolic 24-hour strike on October 22, it has indicated a willingness to continue discussions. By contrast, Micron reached an agreement with its union in Taichung in late October.
The Ministry of Economic Affairs has offered to mediate if required, emphasising that Micron is among the most significant foreign investors in Taiwan.
sentZh: 美國半導體製造商美光科技星期四宣布，其台灣營運運作正常，以回應一篇指稱該公司已暫停在桃園興建新廠計畫的媒體報導。
這篇由彭博社發布的報導指出，一項價值30億至45億美元的擬議投資因勞資糾紛而喊停。
該廠原本要製造先進的記憶體晶片，這是人工智慧系統不可或缺的零組件。
業界觀察人士擔心，這項發展可能使目前全球此類晶片的短缺更加惡化。
值得注意的是，美光的聲明既未證實也未否認暫停一事。
公司表示有信心在不影響客戶的情況下維持桃園的穩定生產，並承諾在市府官員協助下與當地工會進一步協商。
該工會代表桃園3,000名員工中約2,400人，正爭取一項特定的分紅安排。
儘管工會曾在10月22日舉行象徵性的24小時罷工，但已表示願意繼續協商。
相較之下，美光已在10月下旬與台中的工會達成協議。
經濟部表示必要時願意居中協調，並強調美光是台灣最重要的外國投資者之一。

hold.ex: The club wants to hold on to its best players.

hour.ex: The train leaves in an hour.

important.ex: It is important to drink water.

indicated.ex: He indicated that he might leave the company.

industry.ex: Tourism is a key industry in Kerry.

insisted.en: said firmly that something is true
insisted.ex: He insisted that he was right.

intelligence.ex: The intelligence service warned of a cyber attack.

intended.ex: The money is intended for schools.

investors.en: people who put money into businesses
investors.ex: Investors are worried about rising interest rates.

keep.en: to have and not lose; to stay
keep.ex: Keep a torch near the door.

labour.en: the process of giving birth (in labour)
labour.ex: She went into labour at midnight.

larger.ex: They moved to a larger house.

late.en: near the end of the day

leaders.ex: EU leaders will meet in Dublin.

local.ex: The local council runs the park.

machinery.en: machines in general, especially large ones
machinery.ex: The farm bought new machinery this year.

maintaining.en: keeping something at the same level
maintaining.ex: Maintaining good service is our goal.

make.ex: You must make a choice soon.

makes.ex: The company makes software for schools.

manufacture.en: to make goods in a factory
manufacture.ex: The firm will manufacture chips in Taiwan.

manufacturer.ex: The manufacturer opened a new factory.

many.ex: Many people work from home now.

meant.ex: The money is meant to help families.

media.ex: The story spread quickly in the media.

mediate.en: help two sides reach an agreement
mediate.ex: The government offered to mediate between the two sides.

example.en: A judge was asked to mediate between the two companies.
example.zh: 一名法官被請來調解兩家公司的糾紛。

note.usage: 常見 mediate between A and B；mediate a dispute/talks。

noteEn.meaning: to help two sides in a disagreement reach an agreement.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'mediate between A and B', 'mediate a dispute'.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों कंपनियों के बीच मध्यस्थता के लिए एक न्यायाधीश से कहा गया।
noteHi.meaning: विवाद में दोनों पक्षों को समझौते तक पहुँचाने में मदद करना।
noteHi.usage: mediate between A and B आम प्रयोग।

noteEs.exampleTr: Se pidió a un juez que mediara entre las dos empresas.
noteEs.meaning: ayudar a dos partes a llegar a un acuerdo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mediate between A and B.

noteJa.exampleTr: 裁判官が両社の仲裁を依頼された。
noteJa.meaning: 対立する双方の合意を助ける；仲裁する。
noteJa.usage: mediate between A and B の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 한 판사가 두 회사 사이의 중재를 요청받았다.
noteKo.usage: mediate between A and B 형태가 흔하다.

members.en: people who belong to a group

memory.ex: My grandmother has a very good memory.

micron.en: Micron Technology, a US memory-chip maker

ministry.ex: The ministry will announce new rules today.

most.en: used to make the superlative: to the greatest degree
most.ex: This is the most beautiful beach in Spain.

move.ex: The boss refused to move on pay.

municipal.en: of a city or town government
municipal.ex: The municipal library is open on Sundays.

example.en: Municipal officials met the workers on Monday.
example.zh: 市政官員星期一與工人會面。

note.usage: 常見 municipal government/officials/council；比 city 更正式。

noteEn.meaning: relating to a city or town and its local government.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'municipal government', 'municipal officials'; more formal than 'city'.

noteHi.exampleTr: नगर अधिकारियों ने सोमवार को कर्मचारियों से मुलाकात की।
noteHi.meaning: किसी शहर या उसकी स्थानीय सरकार से जुड़ा।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los funcionarios municipales se reunieron con los trabajadores el lunes.
noteEs.meaning: relativo a una ciudad y su gobierno local.

noteJa.exampleTr: 市の職員は月曜日に労働者と面会した。
noteJa.meaning: 市や町とその自治体に関する。

needed.ex: We needed more chairs for the party.

negotiate.ex: The union will negotiate with the firm.

neither.en: not one and not the other
neither.hi: न तो …न; दोनों में से कोई नहीं
neither.zh: neither of them：兩人都沒有；neither…nor：既不…也不

news.ex: I listen to the news every morning.

normal.ex: It looks like a normal pen.

notably.en: clearly; in a way people notice
notably.ex: The weather was notably warmer this week.

example.en: Notably, the report gave no reasons for the change.
example.zh: 值得注意的是，報告並未說明改變的理由。

note.usage: 常放句首表示「值得注意的是」；也可表示 especially。

noteEn.meaning: in a way that is worth noticing; especially.
noteEn.usage: Often used at the start of a sentence: 'Notably, ...'; 'most notably'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Cabe destacar que el informe no explicó el cambio.
noteEs.meaning: de forma digna de atención; especialmente.

noteHi.exampleTr: उल्लेखनीय है कि रिपोर्ट ने बदलाव का कारण नहीं बताया।
noteHi.meaning: ध्यान देने योग्य ढंग से; विशेष रूप से।
noteHi.usage: वाक्य की शुरुआत में Notably, ... आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 注目すべきことに、報告書は変更の理由を示さなかった。
noteJa.meaning: 注目すべきことに；特に。
noteJa.usage: 文頭で Notably, ... の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 주목할 점은 보고서가 변경 이유를 밝히지 않았다는 것이다.

observers.en: people who watch and comment on events

offered.ex: Many families offer rooms to students.

officials.en: people who work for a government
officials.ex: Officials say there is no plan.

on.ex: Voting will go on for nine days.

open.ex: The union is open to new ideas.

particular.ex: Pay particular attention to the last question.

phones.ex: Keep your phones charged in a storm.

plan.en: an idea of what to do
plan.ex: There is no clear plan yet.

planned.ex: The planned trip was cancelled because of rain.

plans.en: ideas for what will be done
plans.ex: The council showed its plans for the park.

pointedly.ja: あからさまに；意図的に
pointedly.en: in a clear and deliberate way
pointedly.ex: He pointedly ignored the reporter's question.

problems.ex: We need to fix these problems.

produce.en: make goods, often in large amounts
produce.ex: The farm produces milk and cheese.

produces.ex: This farm produces milk and cheese.

profit-sharing.en: giving workers part of a company's profits
profit-sharing.ex: The union wants a fair profit-sharing plan for all staff.

profits.en: money a business makes after costs
profits.ex: The company's profits rose sharply this year.

programme.en: a radio or TV show; a course of study
programme.ex: It is my favourite radio programme.

put.en: to place (here: return fish to water)

question.en: something you ask to get an answer
question.ex: The teacher asked a difficult question.

ready.zh: 準備好的（stand ready：隨時準備）

reassure.ex: The bank tried to reassure its customers.

remain.ex: The shops remain closed on Sundays.

remained.ex: The shop remained open all night.

reported.en: said officially; said in the news
reported.ex: Most landlords reported a low income.

represents.ex: This represents a big step forward.

required.ex: You are required to bring ID.
required.zh: 被要求的（be required to：必須）

response.ex: The film got a warm response from critics.

right.en: something you are allowed to do
right.ex: Everyone has the right to vote.

running.ex: The running of a school is costly.

say.ex: Officials say there is no plan.

says.ex: My doctor says I need more sleep.

scheme.en: an official plan from the government

seeking.ex: The president is seeking new funds.

semiconductor.en: material used to make computer chips
semiconductor.ex: Taiwan has a large semiconductor industry.

settled.en: reached an agreement to end a dispute
settled.ex: The two sides settled after long talks.

share.ex: Its share of the market grew.
share.zh: 比例；占有率（market share：市占率）

shelved.ex: The council shelved the plan after protests.

shortage.en: a situation where there is not enough
shortage.ex: There is a shortage of teachers in rural areas.

sides.ex: Both sides want to avoid a strike.

sidestepping.ex: The minister kept sidestepping questions about money.

signalled.en: showed what you think without saying it fully
signalled.ex: The bank signalled that rates could fall.

significant.en: large or important enough to notice
significant.ex: There was a significant rise in prices.

site.en: a place where a building is
site.ex: The hospital moved to a new site.

some.ex: Some fifty people came to the meeting.

sought.en: asked for or tried to get
sought.ex: She sought advice from a lawyer.

special.en: different and given for a reason
special.ex: He got a special prize for effort.

specific.en: clear and exact; about one thing
specific.ex: Please give me a specific date for the meeting.

spend.en: to use money to pay for things
spend.ex: We spend a lot on food each month.

stable.ex: The patient's condition is now stable.

staff.en: the people who work for an organisation

staged.ex: The show was staged in the castle.

statement.ex: The club released a statement this morning.

stating.ex: She left, stating she was tired.

status.en: position or importance in relation to others
status.ex: The city's status as a tech hub is growing.

stoppage.en: a stop in work as a protest

stopped.ex: The company stopped its plans to expand.

strike.ex: Workers went on strike for better pay.

suggesting.ex: Her smile suggested she liked the gift.

suspended.ex: The airline suspended all flights during the storm.
suspended.ja: 一時停止した；凍結した

suspension.ex: The suspension of the service angered users.

example.en: The suspension of the project upset local workers.
example.zh: 該計畫暫停令當地工人不滿。

note.usage: 常見 the suspension of sth；temporary suspension。

noteEn.meaning: the act of stopping something for a period of time.

noteHi.exampleTr: परियोजना के निलंबन से स्थानीय कर्मचारी नाराज़ हुए।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को कुछ समय के लिए रोकना।
noteHi.usage: the suspension of sth आम प्रयोग।

noteEs.exampleTr: La suspensión del proyecto molestó a los trabajadores locales.
noteEs.usage: Se usa the suspension of algo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 計画の停止は地元の労働者を動揺させた。
noteJa.meaning: 一時的に止めること；停止。
noteJa.usage: the suspension of ～ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 프로젝트 중단은 현지 노동자들을 화나게 했다.

sustain.ex: Farms cannot sustain life without water.

example.en: The new factory will sustain 300 local jobs.
example.zh: 新工廠將支撐300個在地工作。

noteEs.exampleTr: La nueva fábrica mantendrá 300 empleos locales.

noteHi.exampleTr: नया कारखाना 300 स्थानीय नौकरियाँ बनाए रखेगा।

noteJa.exampleTr: 新工場は地元の300人の雇用を支える。

noteKo.exampleTr: 새 공장은 지역 일자리 300개를 유지할 것이다.

symbolic.en: having a special meaning that represents something
symbolic.ex: The new bridge is a symbolic link between towns.

systems.en: sets of connected parts that work together
systems.ex: The city upgraded its water systems.

taichung.en: a large city in central Taiwan

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

talk.ex: I need to talk to you about the trip.

talking.ex: The neighbours were talking over the fence.

taoyuan.en: a city in northern Taiwan with the main airport

technology.en: machines and science used in practice

that.en: the one there; used to join clauses

thursday.ex: The meeting is on Thursday afternoon.

trade.en: buying and selling goods and services
trade.ex: Fair trade rules protect small sellers.

unaffected.ex: The north was unaffected by the floods.

underlining.en: showing clearly that something is important
underlining.ex: The data are underlining the need for change.

union's.ex: The union's leaders met the managers.

used.ex: The points are used to give places.

using.ex: The report was made using new data.

walkout.en: a strike where workers leave work
walkout.ex: The pilots staged a walkout over pay.

wants.ex: He wants new money for the EU.

way.ex: There is a new way to pay.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

whose.en: showing that something belongs to the noun before

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

willing.ex: He is willing to help us.

willingness.en: being ready and happy to do something
willingness.ex: There is a willingness to try new ideas.

example.en: Both sides showed a willingness to compromise.
example.zh: 雙方都表現出願意妥協的意願。

note.usage: 常見 willingness to do sth；show/indicate a willingness。

noteEn.meaning: being ready and happy to do something.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'willingness to do something', 'show a willingness'.

noteHi.exampleTr: दोनों पक्षों ने समझौते की इच्छा दिखाई।
noteHi.usage: willingness to do sth आम प्रयोग।

noteEs.exampleTr: Ambas partes mostraron disposición a ceder.

noteJa.exampleTr: 双方とも歩み寄る意欲を示した。
noteJa.meaning: 進んで何かをしようとする気持ち。
noteJa.usage: willingness to do の形が多い。

work.ex: Robots can do some hard work.

workers.ex: The workers asked for a pay rise.

workforce.en: all the workers in a place or sector

world's.ex: The world's tallest building is in Dubai.

worry.en: to feel that something bad may happen
worry.ex: Parents worry about the cost of school.

worse.ex: The traffic is worse than yesterday.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.
